COMPOSITION: a wide, opaque, painted night-time scene filling the whole 16:9 canvas edge to edge. The building is the clear hero: centred, seen from the front in a slight 3/4 view, standing on its ground in the lower part of the frame, nothing cropped. A dirt path leads from the bottom of the frame to its front door. The setting around it sets the scene but stays a little simpler and darker than the building so the building reads first. Night sky.
NO FOG: no mist, haze, fog banks or ground smoke anywhere; the air is perfectly clear and the whole scene is crisp and readable.

1.name: Woods 1: toadstool cottage
1.prefix: The FIRST attached image is the approved Hollow Woods scene and the SECOND its approved house: match their art style, palette, linework, lighting and finish exactly, so this reads as part of the same set. This is a NEW, different house for the same zone (house 1 of 4 in the Hollow Woods; each one is bigger and creepier than the last). The THIRD image is the Goated art style reference.
1.subject: HOLLOW WOODS HOUSE 1 of 4, the smallest and least scary: a small, cosy cottage built inside a giant red-and-white spotted toadstool, a round wooden door, two little round windows glowing warm, a crooked tiny chimney with a wisp of smoke, small mushrooms and ferns around its base. Set in a friendly corner of the enchanted forest: mossy roots, glowing ghostly-green (#02DE82) fireflies and small glowing mushrooms, a crescent moon through the trees. Charming and only lightly spooky. The house takes about 45% of the canvas height.

2.subject: HOLLOW WOODS HOUSE 2 of 4, bigger and a little creepier: a crooked, moss-covered log cabin perched on twisted stilts among huge gnarled roots, a rickety ladder and rope bridge, a lopsided shingled roof, windows glowing ghostly green (#02DE82), hanging lanterns, a crow on the roof and a few cobwebs. Set deeper in the dark forest: taller twisted trees with hanging moss, glowing green mushrooms and fireflies, an owl watching from a branch. The house takes about 55% of the canvas height.

3.subject: HOLLOW WOODS HOUSE 3 of 4, large and creepy: a two-storey manor carved into an enormous ancient hollow oak, its twisted branches reaching out like clawed hands, knotholes that look like watching eyes glowing green (#02DE82), several crooked windows, a heavy arched door, rusty hanging cages and lanterns, bats circling the crown, thick roots coiling across the path. Set in a dark, dense part of the woods with dead twisted trees, thorny brambles, glowing toadstools and green fireflies. The house takes about 65% of the canvas height.

4.subject: HOLLOW WOODS HOUSE 4 of 4, the biggest and creepiest: a towering, gnarled dead-tree fortress with several crooked levels, balconies and pointed witch-hat roofs, huge roots writhing like tentacles, a giant face carved into the trunk with two glowing green (#02DE82) eyes and a wide, toothy open mouth that forms the front doorway, glowing green light inside, a bubbling cauldron of green brew by the door, giant spider webs between the branches, small skull-topped posts along the path, many bats against a large pale moon. Set in the darkest heart of the forest among black dead trees. Very creepy, but spooky-cute, not gory. The house takes about 80% of the canvas height.
